author: National Geographic
description:
Presented by @ROLEX. Pangolins are excellent diggers—they have to be, to get to the tens of thousands of ants and termites a day that make up their diet. National Geographic photographer Marcus Westburg filmed this pangolin at the Tikki Hywood Foundation in Zimbabwe, which works to rehabilitate and rewild these animals, which are among the most trafficked mammals on Earth.  

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about the efforts to save Africa's vanishing pangolins in the October edition of National Geographic: https://on.natgeo.com/347890

author: National Geographic
description:
Journey into the heart of the ancient Middle East to unlock the secrets of the Nabataean Kingdom. In this full episode of Lost Treasures of Arabia from National Geographic, join archaeologists as they excavate the legendary stone-carved cities of Petra and Hegra in modern-day Jordan and Saudi Arabia. Uncover grand architectural marvels, ancient trade networks, and complex urban planning. From intricate burial customs to geopolitical dynamics and the mysterious decline of Hegra, explore how ongoing research is piecing together one of history's most fascinating ancient civilizations.
